{"step":3,"file":"src-vul/libplist/src/oplist.c","function":"node_from_openstep","line":587,"var":"*ctx.pos","code":"if (*ctx->pos == '(') { ... subnode = plist_new_node(data); ... parse_dict_data(ctx, subnode); }","note":"A crafted OpenStep array/dictionary structure causes recursive node construction and nested child insertion."},
{"step":4,"file":"src-vul/libplist/src/oplist.c","function":"parse_dict_data","line":534,"var":"key,val","code":"ctx->err = node_from_openstep(ctx, &key); ... ctx->err = node_from_openstep(ctx, &val);","note":"Dictionary entries are parsed into heap-allocated key/value nodes that become children of the parent plist node."},
{"step":5,"file":"src-vul/libplist/src/oplist.c","function":"plist_from_openstep","line":846,"var":"err","code":"int err = node_from_openstep(&ctx, plist);","note":"On the crashing input, parsing succeeds enough to return a non-NULL root plist tree to the caller."},
{"step":6,"file":"fuzz/oplist_fuzzer.cc","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":29,"var":"root_node","code":"plist_free(root_node);","note":"The fuzzer immediately frees the parsed tree, triggering recursive destruction of the attacker-shaped node graph."},
{"step":7,"file":"src-vul/libplist/src/plist.c","function":"plist_free_node","line":331,"var":"node->parent,node","code":"int node_index = node_detach(node->parent, node);","note":"Freeing a node first detaches it from its parent, mutating sibling/child links while the tree is still being walked."},
{"step":8,"file":"src-vul/libplist/src/plist.c","function":"plist_free_node","line":339,"var":"ch","code":"for (ch = node_first_child(node); ch; ) { node_t *next = node_next_sibling(ch); plist_free_node(ch); ch = next; }","note":"The destructor caches the next sibling before recursing, so later iterations can follow stale pointers after earlier frees."},
{"step":9,"file":"src-vul/libplist/src/plist.c","function":"plist_free_node","line":343,"var":"node","code":"node_destroy(node);","note":"The current node storage is released after its children, completing the use-after-free condition when stale sibling links are dereferenced during traversal."}
]
